Method of Attack: Malicious WinRAR self-extracting archives (SFX) containing harmless decoy files but configured to run PowerShell, Windows command prompt (cmd.exe), and task manager with system privileges via WinRAR’s advanced SFX setup options to open a backdoor
Abuse of utilman.exe accessibility application to launch password-protected SFX files from the logon screen, enabling persistent backdoor access with NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges
Impacted Systems: Windows systems using WinRAR or 7-Zip self-extracting archives
Attack Vector: Password-protected WinRAR SFX archives triggered via utilman.exe on Windows login screen
Use of stolen credentials to plant and execute malicious SFX archives
Indicators of Compromise: Password-protected SFX files containing empty decoy text files but configured to run commands silently without dialogs
Commands to run PowerShell, cmd.exe, and task manager with system privileges embedded in SFX setup
Detection by Microsoft security agent as malicious script tracked as Wacatac (though detection inconsistent)
